cover: A license triage table for your dependencies

slides.title: MIT, Apache 2.0: fine to use
slides.body: Permissive. Keep the copyright and license notice where it's needed. Neither makes you share your own source.

slides.title: GPL: review if you distribute
slides.body: A mobile app, desktop program or device brings its rules in. Code that only runs on your servers generally doesn't.

slides.title: LGPL, MPL 2.0: milder copyleft
slides.body: LGPL: use the library through its interfaces. MPL: share changes to the MPL-licensed files themselves.

slides.title: AGPL: review before adding
slides.body: Network use counts as distribution. Modified AGPL code offered over the web must have its source available to users.

slides.title: SSPL, BSL: read the actual terms
slides.body: Source-available, often restricting commercial hosting. The Open Source Initiative doesn't list them as open source.

slides.title: When to run the list again
slides.body: Before any sale, raise or major customer contract. Have a tool generate it instead of writing it by hand.
